newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian bonds edge up with Friday on their minds.
newsitem.headline: Belgian bonds edge up with Friday on their minds.

text.p: Belgian linear bonds edged higher in thin trading on Wednesday after the overnight rise in New York, but traders said gains would be limited as investors wait for the U.S. jobs figures due on Friday.

"There was relief buying in the U.S. yesterday afternoon, so we have recouped some of our losses. But this is a correction and the real key to the future direction of this market will be the payroll figures on Friday," one trader said.
At 0830 GMT the yield of the benchmark 2007 OLO was 6.10 percent against Tuesday's closing 6.11, and the spread over Bunds was an unchanged 13 basis points.
The June futures contract was 22 basis points higher at 119.25.
ABN-AMRO said in its market commentary on Wednesday the bears were obviously in control at the moment, and bond exchange auctions in the next two weeks would keep a lid on the market.
Kredietbank said in its market commentary that investors were waiting for some price stability to return before coming back into the market.
Traders were mixed over whether the bulk of the more than 60 billion francs in bond coupons that was paid out last Friday had all been reinvested in the bond markets.
"There was some good buying last week, so I think most has come back," one trader said.
However, others said that a fair quantity had moved instead into the money markets for the time being until calm returned to the bond markets.
